timing: Generated records divided by elapsed client time from durable start and completion timestamps. Output manifests, independent Parquet counts and available native rates were cross-checked.
cost: All Slurm GPU allocation seconds, including startup and shutdown, multiplied by the allocated GPU count and divided by 3600.
validation: Post-generation schema validation is separate from this performance comparison. Historical validation audit evidence remains preserved privately.
limitations: Each point represents one observation. The two-node TP8 trials at 2048 and 4096 ran on different scheduling partitions with the same H100 configuration. Each job used one client. Million-record production times are projections.
projection_note: Each four-hour allocation uses its measured pre-client overhead and post-client overhead rounded up to the next second. Capacity rounds down to whole records. Allocation counts round up.
historical_cohort: Results here use a fixed queue limit of 8192 waiting requests per replica. The earlier queue-limit-128 sweeps are excluded.
telemetry: Five-second per-GPU and per-replica samples; ten-second client progress. Token rates use counter deltas. Backend request histograms include server queues and describe completing requests, not full pipeline latency. Both full-client and central60% descriptive windows were checked; central windows do not establish steady state. Proxy diagnostic counts are the last observed counters within each client interval.

runtime_source.status: Isolated experimental build based on release 1.0.0 with only the linked timing and proxy net changes. All other source hashes and dependency versions held fixed; this is historical experimental provenance, not an assertion about a shipped release.

client_concurrency_semantics: Configured per-alias concurrency ceilings, shared across all five model columns. Queue-admission HTTP 429s can trigger client AIMD backoff and deferred retries; the ceiling is not a constant achieved concurrency.

completion_time_projection.method: Array tasks divide the target evenly, with the remainder assigned to the final task. Each task includes measured startup, generation at the measured rate, and shutdown. Jobs start as slots open. The full GPU-hour budget allows four hours per task.
completion_time_projection.limitations: Assumes no queue wait and sustained measured throughput. Excludes retries and collection.

comparison_scope: One 16-CPU client and one proxy per allocation. Compare TP4/TP8 single-client concurrency sweeps on one and two nodes; each projected production job repeats one selected single-client setting.
throughput_metric: All generated output records (schema-valid plus schema-invalid) divided by full durable client runtime. Schema validation does not filter performance rates, GPU cost, or target-record projections.

extension_rule.observed_follow_up: Two-node TP8 at concurrency 4096 was run separately to check whether the throughput increase at 2048 continued.
